title: Wine Wimsey Review · Tue Nov 24
subtitle: NEW-VOICE test batch 2. Replaces the earlier old-style 7+2 Nov 24 batch.json; those PNGs remain in this folder. 8 character feed posts + 2 stories. All posts use the locked cartoon character with a rotating expression and an action. Captions and first comments included. No TOBIs, no plain cards. Seasonal: none. Quotes: 10 original. Credits: GenerateImage (free). Scott accepted all 8 feed posts and 2 stories and said upload them all on Nov 23. First-comment delays randomized (mix of 0 and 1-20 minutes). Posting time blank so posts fill Scott's staggered Post Planner queue slots.

posts.quote: Call me crazy, but a $38 'convenience fee' / for a ticket I printed at home / isn't convenient for anybody but them.
posts.caption: Forty-two dollars for the seat, thirty-eight to 'process' it, and four-fifty more so I could print it on my own paper with my own ink. Barb says just stay home. Barb might be right.
posts.first: I bought them anyway, of course. I'm just going to complain the whole drive there.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses at a kitchen table at night. She squints with her mouth open and jabs a finger at a laptop that says SERVICE FEE $38.00, with a glass of red wine beside her. Text at the top reads: Call me crazy, but a $38 'convenience fee' for a ticket I printed at home. A pink box at the bottom reads: Isn't convenient for anybody but them.
posts.note: new-voice batch 2, approved via upload Nov 23
posts.expression: open-mouth 'are you kidding me' squint, jabbing a finger at the laptop

posts.quote: When I was a kid, a birthday party was cake, a paper hat, and pin the tail on the donkey. / Now it's a $600 bounce house / and goodie bags nicer than my purse.
posts.caption: My parties were a card table in the basement and one balloon tied to the mailbox so people could find the house. Everybody went home happy and a little sticky.
posts.first: My niece's little one came home with a goodie bag that had a water bottle in it. I'm still drinking out of a jar.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration in two panels. 1979: a smiling younger woman in a polka-dot party hat sits with a cake, a donkey poster on the wall. Now: a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses holds up a shiny goodie bag with a tight fake smile, a bounce house behind her. Text at the top reads: When I was a kid, a birthday party was cake, a paper hat, and pin the tail on the donkey. Now it's a $600 bounce house. A teal box at the bottom reads: And goodie bags nicer than my purse.
posts.note: new-voice batch 2, approved via upload Nov 23
posts.expression: tight fake 'everything is fine' smile, holding up a shiny goodie bag like evidence

posts.quote: If you're going to text me 'Can I call you?' / just call me. / That's what the phone part is for.
posts.caption: It now takes three messages to set up one phone call that would've taken two minutes. We're all so busy texting about talking that nobody actually talks.
posts.first: My sister does this every single time. I answer with a phone call just to make a point.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses, shown close up on a yellow background. She raises one eyebrow in a smirk and holds up a phone showing a text that says Can I call you? Text at the top reads: If you're going to text me 'Can I call you?' just call me. A red box at the bottom reads: That's what the phone part is for.
posts.note: new-voice batch 2, approved via upload Nov 23
posts.expression: one raised eyebrow smirk, holding the phone up to show the 'Can I call you?' text

posts.quote: I pay for three streaming services. / All three raised the price. / Two added commercials. / Congratulations, I'm paying for cable again.
posts.caption: I signed up so I could skip commercials. Now the cheap plan has commercials and the old plan costs what cable used to. Somewhere a cable company is laughing.
posts.first: I cancelled one last month. They've emailed me four times begging me to come back.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses on a living room couch at night. She rolls her eyes and aims a remote at a TV that says PRICE INCREASE, with a glass of red wine on the side table. Text at the top reads: I pay for three streaming services. All three raised the price. Two added commercials. A purple box at the bottom reads: Congratulations, I'm paying for cable again.
posts.note: new-voice batch 2, approved via upload Nov 23
posts.expression: eye-roll, aiming the remote at the 'PRICE INCREASE' screen

posts.quote: In 1985 the mechanic listened for ten seconds and said, 'Alternator.' / Now it's $189 to plug in a computer and tell me my check engine light is on. / I know. That's why I came.
posts.caption: Gary down the road could hear a bad belt from the driveway. Charged you twenty bucks and told you to go get a coffee while he fixed it.
posts.first: Gary retired years ago. My car has been mad at me ever since.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration in two panels. 1985: a smiling mechanic listens under an open hood, a younger woman in a green cardigan beside him. Now: a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses pulls her glasses down and side-eyes a blank invoice. Text at the top reads: In 1985 the mechanic listened for ten seconds and said, 'Alternator.' Now it's $189 to plug in a computer and tell me my check engine light is on. An orange box at the bottom reads: I know. That's why I came.
posts.note: new-voice batch 2, approved via upload Nov 23
posts.expression: side-eye over glasses pulled down her nose, holding the invoice

posts.quote: Turn signals come standard on every car. / They are not an upgrade. / Use the blinker, Kevin.
posts.caption: Two lanes over, no blinker, inches off my bumper. Then he waved at me like we were old friends. We are not friends, Kevin.
posts.first: I don't actually know his name. Every driver like that is a Kevin to me.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses, shown close up on a light blue background. She grimaces with gritted teeth, both hands gripping the steering wheel. Text at the top reads: Turn signals come standard on every car. They are not an upgrade. A pink box at the bottom reads: Use the blinker, Kevin.
posts.note: new-voice batch 2, approved via upload Nov 23
posts.expression: twitchy gritted-teeth grimace, both hands strangling the steering wheel

posts.quote: You walked every aisle in the store. / The cart corral is thirty feet away. / You'll live.
posts.caption: Watched a man leave his cart wedged against my door, then sit in his truck scrolling his phone for ten minutes. He had time. He had all the time in the world.
posts.first: I pushed it back for him. Very slowly, right past his window.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses in a parking lot, a lime glow around her, one hand on her hip, pointing at a man scrolling his phone by a truck, with a shopping cart left beside a blue car. Text at the top reads: You walked every aisle in the store. The cart corral is thirty feet away. A teal box at the bottom reads: You'll live.
posts.note: new-voice batch 2, approved via upload Nov 23
posts.expression: smug satisfied smirk, hand on hip, pointing at the guy on his phone

posts.quote: It was a 'free' trial. / Signing up took one click. / Canceling takes a phone call, Monday to Friday, 9 to 4. / Funny how that works.
posts.caption: Signing up took one click. Canceling took a phone number, a hold song, and a nice young man who asked me three times if I was sure. I was sure.
posts.first: I still got charged once before it went through. Calendar reminder set for next time.
